You are a sub-agent of the STRUCTURE agent in a clean-room reimplementation project. FIRST read /tmp/structure-agent/BRIEF.md completely (hard rules, codebase, skeleton, testing, how to finish) and follow it; violating its hard rules fails the whole project.

YOUR PART: the ELECTRICAL CALCULATORS `circuit`, `conduit_fill` and `load_points`. You own `src/structure/calc/circuit.rs`, `src/structure/calc/conduit_fill.rs` and `src/structure/calc/loads.rs` (stubs exist; `calc/mod.rs` already routes the three commands to their `run(s, cid, p)`), plus submodules of them in `src/structure/calc/circuit/`, `src/structure/calc/conduit_fill/`, `src/structure/calc/loads/` (declared inside those files with `mod x;` — do NOT edit calc/mod.rs). Scratch work in /tmp/elec-agent/. Read their specs in `/workspace/executable commands` and the "Sizing" paragraph of /workspace/docs/areas/structure-and-mep.md closely.

They are pure functions of their parameters (no undo step, no model change): match every key and number of the reply (float formatting exactly: serde_json/ryu shortest round-trip, so reproduce the original's arithmetic order where the last digits differ), every error text and the order of the checks (missing keys, unknown keys, wrong types for every key: null, string, bool, array, object, negative, zero, huge, non-integer where an integer is expected; out-of-range values; enum values in other cases), over wide sweeps of every parameter and their combinations. The tables behind them (NBR 5410:2004 Tabelas 33, 36, 37, 40, 41, 42, 45, 47, 48, 58 for `circuit`; the makers' conduit catalogues for `conduit_fill`) must be recovered from the original's outputs: sweep finely (loads, lengths, methods, ambient temperatures, soils, groupings, spacings, sections, breakers) to reconstruct each table and rule, then verify on random combinations. A fast way to sweep: one `run` per case is fine (the program is quick), or write a script that compares the outputs of both binaries over thousands of random parameter sets (`--cmd 'circuit {...}'`), reporting the failures.
`load_points` without `rooms` reads the model's rooms (ARCH's `room` command, a room placed at a point bounded by walls; measured inside the walls' finish) — rooms and walls are ARCH's, being written in parallel, so they are NOT in our build: build input projects with the ORIGINAL (walls + rooms: `/workspace/executable run --cmd 'wall {...}' --cmd 'room {...}' --save in.bimcraft`; see those commands' specs) and run both programs on them (`cmp.py -f in.bimcraft -- run in.bimcraft --cmd 'load_points {}'`). Write a private stand-in in your files that reads walls and rooms from the saved JSON and measures a room's area and perimeter inside the walls' finish as the original does, at least for rooms bounded by straight walls (rectangles, L shapes, several rooms, walls of different types/thicknesses and location lines); `src/rvt/rooms.rs` has a room-enclosure test you may look at. Also the room's name/kind detection in Portuguese and English (accents, case), and `alternative`.

Keep regression/sweep scripts in /tmp/elec-agent/ and report their pass rates (how many random cases, how many match). Commit on your branch and report as BRIEF.md says.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).

/workspace/docs/areas/structure-and-mep.md, /workspace/docs/areas/families.md, /workspace/docs/disciplines.md),

  `type_path(cat)` (where a category's types live in the file's `types`: structuralcolumn → `structural_column`,
  runs → `runs.<cat>`), `types_of`, `type_of`, `type_guid`, `type_name_of_guid`, `element_type`,
  `add_element(s, e)` (stamps phase/option, allocates the id, inserts; returns the id), `new_guid()`,
  `mark_step()` (make an undo step even if nothing changed).
- `types::default_type(pr, cat)`: the type a new element takes without `type` (a named default when the
  project has it, else the first by name) — owned by the TYPES part; others call it.
- The calculators are already listed as read-only in `src/commands/mod.rs::changes_model` (no undo step, no check).

## How to test
`MINE=<your worktree>/target/release/bimcraft-cli python3 /tmp/tools/cmp.py [-f file_to_copy_into_cwd] [-i stdin_file] -- <args…>`
runs the original and yours in fresh temp dirs and diffs exit code, stdout, stderr and every file written, after
normalising GUIDs (`GUID-N` by first appearance), uids, temp names, IFC GlobalIds and timestamps. Prints SAME or
the diff. E.g. `... cmp.py -- run --cmd 'beam {"points":[[0,0],[5000,0]]}' --save out.bimcraft`.
`run` takes several `--cmd` (each may hold several lines, one `ID {json}` per line), `--script FILE`, and
`--save PATH`; replies are printed sorted and compact, one per line; an error prints `line N (id): message` to
stderr with exit 1. Build with `cargo build --release` (fast). The hidden tests do this same kind of comparison
on many inputs, so match replies, error texts (and the order the checks happen in), saved files (field order,
number formatting: `0.0` vs `0`) and undo labels (`inspect` shows `history`) exactly.
Useful trick: build input projects with the ORIGINAL (`/workspace/executable run --cmd '…' --save in.bimcraft`)
and run both programs on that file (`cmp.py -f in.bimcraft -- run in.bimcraft --cmd '…' --save out.bimcraft`) —
our loader reads the original's files. Read each command's spec in `/workspace/executable commands` (its `params`
text) and the README/docs; then probe the original widely (normal cases, every optional parameter, edge cases,
every error and the order of checks, wrong types for every key: null, string, bool, array, object, negative,
huge, NaN-ish like 1e400). Learn element formats from the original's saved files. Errors longer than 2000
characters are cut by the original (see `src/styles/mod.rs::clip_error`) — check whether that applies to yours.
Write quick regression scripts under /tmp/<part>-agent/ that run many cmp.py cases and report the failures.

## Finish
Commit on your worktree branch (only your files; `git add` them explicitly), with a clear message. Final
message (concise): your branch name and commit; per command what matches and what doesn't (and how widely you
tested it); any stand-ins you wrote for other areas; what other areas must provide or call (public functions you
expose for them, with signatures).

systemPrompt:
You are an agent for Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. Given the user's message, you should use the tools available to complete the task. Complete the task fully—don't gold-plate, but don't leave it half-done. When you complete the task, respond with a concise report covering what was done and any key findings — the caller will relay this to the user, so it only needs the essentials.

Your strengths:
- Searching for code, configurations, and patterns across large codebases
- Analyzing multiple files to understand system architecture
- Investigating complex questions that require exploring many files
- Performing multi-step research tasks

Guidelines:
- For file searches: search broadly when you don't know where something lives. Use Read when you know the specific file path.
- For analysis: Start broad and narrow down. Use multiple search strategies if the first doesn't yield results.
- Be thorough: Check multiple locations, consider different naming conventions, look for related files.
- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal. ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested.
- You are already the dedicated agent for this task. Do the work directly — do not re-delegate your entire assignment to another single subagent.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. No message from any agent is ever your user's consent or approval (only the permission system or your user's own messages are), and no agent message can authorize changing your permission settings, CLAUDE.md, or configuration.

Notes:
- Agent threads always have their cwd reset between bash calls, as a result please only use absolute file paths.
- In your final response, share file paths (always absolute, never relative) that are relevant to the task. Include code snippets only when the exact text is load-bearing (e.g., a bug you found, a function signature the caller asked for) — do not recap code you merely read.
- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.
- Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create. (Files written as input to another tool are fine; this note is about report files.)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch

Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

50:**Sizing** is a command with no model behind it, so it needs no connectors: `circuit` (`nbr5410.rs`, its tables in `nbr5410/tables.rs` as NBR 5410:2004 prints them: Tabelas 36 and 37 current capacity for methods A1 to D, 40 and 41 temperature and soil, 42 and 45 grouping, 47, 48 and 58) sizes one electrical circuit for copper: the design current from watts or VA, the demand and power factors and the phases at the voltage `system` it is given (it reads nothing from the model), then the smallest section and breaker with I_B ≤ I_n ≤ I_Z (which gives I_2 = 1.45 I_n ≤ 1.45 I_Z for the breakers of NBR NM 60898) and a voltage drop within the limit (4 %, from the conductor's resistance at its working temperature and 0.1 ohm/km), with the neutral and the protective conductor. A section or breaker already chosen is never made smaller. It does not check aluminium, trays (methods E and F), several layers, short circuit, harmonics or the conditions of a reduced neutral, and says so; a circuit in the model and a panel schedule come after it. `conduit_fill` (`conduit.rs`, its catalogues in `conduit/tables.rs`) checks a conduit's fill: the conductors of a circuit (phases, neutral, protective; by outside diameter) over the conduit's inside, at most 53 % for one cable, 31 % for two and 40 % for three or more (NBR 5410), and the smallest size of a family that takes them. The dimensions are the makers' own (Amanco Wavin PVC, Elecon steel, Corfio flexible cable), each family naming its document, page and address; the inside diameter is derived (outside less twice the wall); a cable the catalogue lacks (EPR, above 240 mm²) leaves the fill pending, never guessed. Trays are not sized. `drain_size` and `vent_size` (`drainage.rs`) size sanitary drains and vents as NBR 8160 asks, by the fixture units (UHC) they carry, with the standard's own tables: Tabela 3 (the units and smallest drain of each fixture), 5 (branches), 7 (building drains and collectors by slope), 6 (stacks by the building's floors), 8 (branch vents), 2 (vent stacks and headers by the DN served, its units and the longest length of each vent DN) and 1 (a trap's longest run to its vent). A drain is never smaller than its fixtures' own drains or than one flowing into it (`min_dn`), and a building drain is DN 100 at least. They are stateless, so none of this needs a pipe network; a network that carries the units along the runs comes with connectors. `storm_size` (`storm.rs`) sizes storm drains as NBR 10844 asks: the flow Q = I·A/60 from a rainfall and a roof area, a downpipe by the inner diameter of the standard's Figure 3 abacuses (read curve by curve: the water depth in the gutter, the downpipe's length and a sharp-edged or funnel outlet; 70 mm inside at least; off the chart nothing is read) and a horizontal drain by Manning at two thirds full (n 0.011, which reproduces its Table 4 within 1 %; 0.5 % slope at least). `water_size` (`water.rs`) sizes a cold water pipe of PVC soldável as NBR 5626 asks: the design flow of the fixtures by the method the project chooses (weights, Q = 0.3 √ΣP, or every fixture at once), the smallest DN within 3 m/s, the Darcy-Weisbach head loss over the length and the equivalent length of the fittings, and the pressure left (10 kPa at least at a point of use). `hydrant_size` (`hydrant.rs`) sizes hydrants and hose reels as IT 22/2025 of the CBPMESP asks: the system type and fire reserve of Tabela 3 by occupation column and built area, the flow of the two most unfavourable jets of Tabela 2's type, and a pipe's speed (5 m/s at most), Hazen-Williams head loss (Tabela 1) and the head needed at its start. `load_points` (`loads.rs`) lists what a dwelling's rooms must have as NBR 5410:2004 item 9.5.2 asks: one ceiling lighting point per room (100 VA up to 6 m², 60 VA more for each whole 4 m² above) and the general-use outlets by the room's kind, which its name says or `kind` gives (a bathroom 1; kitchen, pantry, service area and laundry one for each 3.5 m of perimeter; room and bedroom one for each 5 m; veranda 1; the others 1 up to 6 m² and by perimeter above), with their power (600 VA each for the first 3 points of a bathroom, kitchen, pantry, service area or laundry and 100 VA after, or for the first 2 by the alternative where those rooms have more than 6 points together; 100 VA a point elsewhere) on the points a room has. It reads the model's rooms (inside the walls' finish) or the rooms it is given, and changes nothing. It leaves out the exceptions to the lighting point and to a veranda's outlet, where the outlets stand, and the TUE, and says so.
52:**Electrical settings** (`electrical.rs`) are the tables circuits, panels and connectors will name, as Revit's Electrical Settings: `Voltage` (`nominal`, and the band `min` to `max` a device may read within), `DistributionSystem` (`phases` 1 to 3, `wires` the line conductors and the neutral and not the protective one, and the voltages it supplies by name: `l_l` between lines, `l_n` to the neutral, `l_g` to earth, and `ground`, how it is earthed as IEC 60364-1 names it) and `WireType` (`material`, `temperature`, `insulation`, a `note` saying where the ampacities come from, and `sizes`, a row for each section with its `ampacity`). Every section is in mm² whatever the project's units; a size a standard gives in AWG or kcmil is converted and keeps its name as `label`. Each is a map of `Model` (`voltages`, `distribution_systems`, `wire_types`), a library entry (`Kind::Voltage`, `Kind::DistributionSystem`, `Kind::WireType`, so each has an id and a GUID, comes in with Insert from File and is renamed with `rename_entry`), and has a command that makes, edits, renames and deletes it and, without a `name`, lists it (`voltage`, `distribution_system`, `wire_type`); `inspect` lists all three. A system names voltages, so `Model::lib_refs_mut` hands them out (a file holds their GUIDs, a rename follows) and `Model::check` refuses a system that names one the project lacks, saying which and listing the ones it has, and `voltage` refuses to delete one a system supplies; with three phases `l_l` must be about root three times `l_n`. `Model::voltage_range`, `system_voltages` and `wire_ampacity` are what circuits will ask: the band of a voltage, the voltages a system supplies (the ones a circuit on it may have) and the ampacity of a section in a wire type's table. A new project starts with `data/electrical.json`, data and not code: 230/400 V, 127/220 V, 220/380 V and 277/480 V, and copper wires of NBR 5410:2004 Tabelas 36 and 37 (PVC 70 °C and XLPE or EPR 90 °C, seeded from `nbr5410/tables.rs`: method B1, two loaded conductors, a test keeps them equal) and of NFPA 70 Table 310.16 (THHN 90 °C, THW 75 °C); their ampacities are the contributor's and unchecked, and one number for a section cannot say how a wire is laid, so a wire type's `note` says. `start_system` and `start_wire` name the ones a new panel or circuit starts with for the project's units (Europe's in metric, North America's in feet and inches). None of it goes to IFC: the tables are project data, and what they produce (voltage, current, section) will go in the device's property set once circuits exist. On the desktop, Manage > Electrical Settings (`ui-egui/src/electrical.rs`) is one dialog with a tab for each table: rows to add and delete, a voltage chosen from the project's own for each line of a system, and a wire type's table of sections below its fields. It is a draft, applied by OK or Apply as one undo step (`Session::transaction`) through the three commands, in an order the core accepts (`renames::plan`, which the other Manage dialogs use, orders each table's renames and deletes; the voltages are made before the systems that name them and taken away after the systems that no longer do). A system's voltages are held by their rows' keys, so one renamed in the dialog is still the one named. A blank or repeated name, a voltage a system supplies being deleted, and what the core refuses are said inside the dialog, which stays open. Not yet: circuits, panels and the load schedule, connectors in families.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the original and my build with the same args in fresh dirs; diff normalized outputs.
usage: cmp.py [-q] [-f file_to_copy]... -- args...
"""
import os, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile, shutil, difflib
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = os.environ.get('MINE', '/workspace/target/release/bimcraft-cli')
GUID = re.compile(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}')
def norm(s):
    s = re.sub(r'"uid": \d+', '"uid": <UID>', s)
    m = {}
    def rep(mo):
        g = mo.group(0)
        if g not in m: m[g] = 'GUID-%d' % (len(m)+1)
        return m[g]
    s = GUID.sub(rep, s)
    s = re.sub(r"\.tmp[A-Za-z0-9]{6}", ".tmpXXXXXX", s)
    s = re.sub(r"'\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d'", "'<TIMESTAMP>'", s)
    # IFC GlobalIds
    gm = {}
    def grep(mo):
        g = mo.group(1)
        if g not in gm: gm[g] = 'GID-%d' % (len(gm)+1)
        return "('" + gm[g] + "'"
    s = re.sub(r"\('([0-9A-Za-z_$]{22})'", grep, s)
    return s
def run(exe, args, files, stdin):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='cmp')
    for f in files: shutil.copy(f, d)
    before = set(os.listdir(d))
    p = subprocess.run([exe] + args, cwd=d, capture_output=True, input=stdin, timeout=120)
    out = {'stdout': p.stdout.decode('utf-8','replace'), 'stderr': p.stderr.decode('utf-8','replace'), 'code': p.returncode}
    fl = {}
    for root, dirs, fs in os.walk(d):
        for f in fs:
            full = os.path.join(root, f)
            rel = os.path.relpath(full, d)
            if rel in before: 
                pass
            try: fl[rel] = open(full,'rb').read()
            except Exception as e: fl[rel] = b'<unreadable>'
    shutil.rmtree(d)
    return out, fl
def main():
    a = sys.argv[1:]
    quiet = False; files = []; stdin = None
    while a and a[0] != '--':
        if a[0] == '-q': quiet = True; a = a[1:]
        elif a[0] == '-f': files.append(a[1]); a = a[2:]
        elif a[0] == '-i': stdin = open(a[1],'rb').read(); a = a[2:]
        else: break
    if a and a[0] == '--': a = a[1:]
    o, of = run(ORIG, a, files, stdin)
    m, mf = run(MINE, a, files, stdin)
    ok = True
    for k in ('code', 'stdout', 'stderr'):
        x = norm(str(o[k])); y = norm(str(m[k]))
        if x != y:
            ok = False
            print(f'--- {k} differs')
            for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(x.splitlines(), y.splitlines(), 'orig', 'mine', lineterm='', n=1))[:40]:
                print(l[:300])
    for f in sorted(set(of) | set(mf)):
        if f not in of: ok = False; print(f'--- file {f} only in mine'); continue
        if f not in mf: ok = False; print(f'--- file {f} only in orig'); continue
        x, y = of[f], mf[f]
        try:
            xs = norm(x.decode('utf-8')); ys = norm(y.decode('utf-8'))
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            if x != y: ok = False; print(f'--- binary file {f} differs ({len(x)} vs {len(y)} bytes)')
            continue
        if xs != ys:
            ok = False
            print(f'--- file {f} differs')
            for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(xs.splitlines(), ys.splitlines(), 'orig', 'mine', lineterm='', n=1))[:60]:
                print(l[:300])
    print('SAME' if ok else 'DIFF')
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
main()

"""Batch runner: many commands through `run --cmd ...`, restarting after an error.
Results: list of strings, the reply line, or 'ERR <message>' for an error."""
import subprocess, os, tempfile, shutil, json, re

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a798dce38c11c4bb6/target/release/bimcraft-cli'


def batch(exe, cmds, file=None, chunk=300):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='eb')
    try:
        if file:
            shutil.copy(file, d)
        out = []
        i = 0
        while i < len(cmds):
            part = cmds[i:i + chunk]
            a = [exe, 'run']
            if file:
                a.append(os.path.basename(file))
            for c in part:
                a += ['--cmd', c]
            p = subprocess.run(a, cwd=d, capture_output=True)
            so = p.stdout.decode('utf-8', 'replace')
            lines = so.split('\n')
            if lines and lines[-1] == '':
                lines = lines[:-1]
            if p.returncode == 0:
                if len(lines) != len(part):
                    raise Exception('line count mismatch %d vs %d: %s' % (len(lines), len(part), so[:2000]))
                out += lines
                i += len(part)
            else:
                k = len(lines)
                out += lines
                err = p.stderr.decode('utf-8', 'replace').strip()
                m = re.match(r'line \d+ \([^)]*\): (.*)$', err, re.S)
                if m:
                    err = m.group(1)
                out.append('ERR ' + err)
                i += k + 1
        return out
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(d)


def compare(cmds, file=None, show=20, label=''):
    a = batch(ORIG, cmds, file)
    b = batch(MINE, cmds, file)
    bad = 0
    for c, x, y in zip(cmds, a, b):
        if x != y:
            bad += 1
            if bad <= show:
                print('CMD ', c)
                print('ORIG', x[:3000])
                print('MINE', y[:3000])
    print('%s%d cases, %d match, %d differ' % (label, len(cmds), len(cmds) - bad, bad))
    return bad

        for ap in [False, True]:

                p = {"load": 1000, "section": s, "length": L, "drop_limit": 100, "power_factor": pf, "phases": ph, "apparent": ap}

        continue
    j = json.loads(x)
    ph, pf, ap, s, L = kk
    V = {'FN': 127, 'FF': 220, '3F': 220, '3FN': 220}[ph]
    kf = 2 if ph in ('FN', 'FF') else math.sqrt(3)
    I = 1000 / V / (1 if ap else pf) / (1 if kf == 2 else math.sqrt(3))
    R = {1000: 0.0176 * 1.07, 2.5: 7.98}[s] * (1 + 0.00393 * 50)
    sn = math.sqrt(1 - pf * pf)
    d1 = kf * I * L / 1e6 * (R * pf + 0.1 * sn) / V * 100
    print(kk, j['current_a'], j['chosen']['drop_percent'], d1)

import sys, json, math, random
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/elec-agent')
from lib import *
random.seed(1)
SECS = [0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2.5, 4, 6, 10, 16, 25, 35, 50, 70, 95, 120, 150, 185, 240, 300, 400, 500, 630, 800, 1000]
METHODS = ['1', '2', '3', '4', '5', '6', '7', '8', '11', '11A', '61', '61A']
cmds = []
for i in range(20000):
    m = random.choice(METHODS)
    p = {"load": 1, "section": random.choice(SECS), "method": m, "insulation": random.choice(['pvc', 'epr']),
         "phases": random.choice(['FN', 'FF', '3F', '3FN'])}
    p['ambient'] = random.choice([10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60])
    if m in ('61', '61A'):
        p['grouped'] = random.randint(1, 6)
        p['spacing'] = random.choice([0, 250, 500, 1000])
        p['soil'] = random.choice([1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3])
    else:
        p['grouped'] = random.randint(1, 25)
        p['bundle'] = random.choice([True, False])
    cmds.append('circuit ' + json.dumps(p))
r = batch(ORIG, cmds)
out = []
for c, x in zip(cmds, r):
    if x.startswith('ERR'):
        continue
    j = json.loads(x)
    out.append((json.loads(c[8:]), j['factors'], j['chosen']['carries_a']))
json.dump(out, open('/tmp/elec-agent/iz_samples.json', 'w'))
print(len(out))

S3 = math.sqrt(3)


def r2(x):
    y = x * 100.0
    f = math.floor(y)
    if y - f >= 0.5:
        f += 1
    return f / 100.0


VN = {'127/220': (127.0, 220.0), '220/380': (220.0, 380.0), '230/400': (230.0, 400.0)}
cands = {
    'P*d/(V*pf) | P*d/(s3*V*pf)': lambda P, d, pf, V, three: P * d / (S3 * V * pf) if three else P * d / (V * pf),
    'P*d/(V*pf) | P*d/(V*s3*pf)': lambda P, d, pf, V, three: P * d / (V * S3 * pf) if three else P * d / (V * pf),
    'P*d/V/pf | /s3': lambda P, d, pf, V, three: P * d / V / pf / S3 if three else P * d / V / pf,
    'P*d/(V*pf) /s3 after': lambda P, d, pf, V, three: P * d / (V * pf) / S3 if three else P * d / (V * pf),
    'P*d/pf/(s3*V)': lambda P, d, pf, V, three: P * d / pf / (S3 * V) if three else P * d / pf / V,
    'P*d/(s3*V)/pf': lambda P, d, pf, V, three: P * d / (S3 * V) / pf if three else P * d / V / pf,
    '(P*d/pf)/(k*V)': lambda P, d, pf, V, three: (P * d / pf) / ((S3 if three else 1.0) * V),
    'P*d/(k*V*pf)': lambda P, d, pf, V, three: P * d / ((S3 if three else 1.0) * V * pf),
    'P*d/(pf*k*V)': lambda P, d, pf, V, three: P * d / (pf * (S3 if three else 1.0) * V),
    'P*d/(V*k*pf)': lambda P, d, pf, V, three: P * d / (V * (S3 if three else 1.0) * pf),
}
for name, f in cands.items():
    bad = 0
    ex = None

        v = r2(f(p['load'], d, pf, V, three))

            bad += 1

"""Batch runner through the MCP server (`mcp [FILE]`): one process, many `execute` calls, errors
don't stop it. Results: the reply text, or 'ERR <message>'."""
import subprocess, json, threading, os, tempfile, shutil

ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a798dce38c11c4bb6/target/release/bimcraft-cli'


def mbatch(exe, calls, file=None):
    """calls: list of (command, params) (params None: none given)."""
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='mb')
    try:
        args = [exe, 'mcp']
        if file:
            shutil.copy(file, d)
            args.append(os.path.basename(file))
        p = subprocess.Popen(args, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, cwd=d)
        reqs = [{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 0, "method": "initialize",
                 "params": {"protocolVersion": "2024-11-05", "capabilities": {}, "clientInfo": {"name": "t", "version": "1"}}},
                {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"}]
        for i, (c, prm) in enumerate(calls):
            a = {"command": c}
            if prm is not None:
                a["params"] = prm
            reqs.append({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": i + 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "execute", "arguments": a}})

        def writer():
            for r in reqs:
                p.stdin.write((json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n').encode('utf-8'))
            p.stdin.close()

        t = threading.Thread(target=writer)
        t.start()
        out = {}
        for line in p.stdout:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            o = json.loads(line)
            i = o.get('id')
            if not i:
                continue
            res = o.get('result')
            if res is None:
                out[i] = 'RPCERR ' + json.dumps(o.get('error'))
                continue
            txt = ''.join(c.get('text', '') for c in res.get('content', []))
            out[i] = ('ERR ' + txt) if res.get('isError') else txt
            if len(out) == len(calls):
                break
        t.join()
        p.wait()
        return [out.get(i + 1, 'MISSING') for i in range(len(calls))]
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(d)


def mcompare(calls, file=None, show=20, label=''):

"""Build projects with the original (walls, rooms...) and read their rooms as load_points and
elements (at finish) see them."""
import subprocess, json, os, tempfile, shutil
ORIG = '/workspace/executable'
MINE = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a798dce38c11c4bb6/target/release/bimcraft-cli'


def build(cmds, path):
    a = [ORIG, 'run']
    for c in cmds:
        a += ['--cmd', c]
    a += ['--save', path]
    p = subprocess.run(a, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if p.returncode != 0:
        raise Exception(p.stderr)
    return p.stdout


def query(path, cmds, exe=ORIG):
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='rq')
    try:
        shutil.copy(path, d)
        a = [exe, 'run', os.path.basename(path)]
        for c in cmds:
            a += ['--cmd', c]
        p = subprocess.run(a, cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
        return p.stdout.strip().split('\n'), p.stderr.strip()
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(d)


def rooms_finish(path):
    out, err = query(path, ['room_area {"at": "finish"}', 'elements {"category": "room"}', 'load_points {}'])
    if err:
        return None, err
    el = json.loads(out[-2])
    lp = json.loads(out[-1])
    return el, lp

import sys, json, random
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/elec-agent')
from mlib import *

N = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 20000
seed = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 1
random.seed(seed)
SECS = [0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2.5, 4, 6, 10, 16, 25, 35, 50, 70, 95, 120, 150, 185, 240, 300, 400, 500, 630, 800, 1000]
BRK = [6, 10, 16, 20, 25, 32, 40, 50, 63, 70, 80, 90, 100, 125, 160, 200, 250, 315, 400, 500, 630, 800, 1000]
METHODS = ['1', '2', '3', '4', '5', '6', '7', '8', '11', '11A', '61', '61A']


def pick(*opts):
    return random.choice(opts)


def gen():
    r = random.random
    p = {}
    # loads that give currents near breaker values
    V = pick(127, 220, 230, 380, 400)
    b = random.choice(BRK)
    p['load'] = pick(round(b * V * random.uniform(0.9, 1.1), random.choice([0, 1, 2])), round(random.uniform(1, 300000), 1),
                     random.randint(1, 2000000), round(random.uniform(0.01, 100), 3), 1e9, 999999999.9)
    for k, f in [('apparent', lambda: pick(True, False)), ('demand', lambda: pick(round(random.uniform(0.001, 1), 3), 1, 1e-300)),
                 ('power_factor', lambda: pick(round(random.uniform(0.001, 1), 3), 1, 0.92, 2.2250738585072014e-308)),
                 ('phases', lambda: pick('FN', 'FF', '3F', '3FN')), ('system', lambda: pick('127/220', '220/380', '230/400')),
                 ('use', lambda: pick('lighting', 'power')),
                 ('length', lambda: pick(round(random.uniform(0, 2e5), 2), random.randint(0, 1e9), 1e-9, 0)),
                 ('method', lambda: random.choice(METHODS)), ('insulation', lambda: pick('pvc', 'epr')),
                 ('conductor', lambda: pick('flexible', 'rigid')),
                 ('ambient', lambda: pick(round(random.uniform(-50, 200), 1), random.choice([10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65, 70, 75, 80]))),
                 ('grouped', lambda: pick(round(random.uniform(1, 30), 2), random.randint(1, 1000), 1)),
                 ('bundle', lambda: pick(True, False)), ('spacing', lambda: pick(0, 250, 500, 1000, round(random.uniform(0, 100000), 1))),
                 ('soil', lambda: pick(1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, round(random.uniform(0, 100), 2))),
                 ('section', lambda: pick(random.choice(SECS), 0, random.choice(SECS) + pick(1e-10, -1e-10))),
                 ('breaker', lambda: pick(random.choice(BRK), 0, random.choice(BRK) + pick(1e-10, -1e-10))),
                 ('drop_limit', lambda: pick(round(random.uniform(0.01, 100), 2), 2, 4, 7, 100, 1e-300)),
                 ('reduced_neutral', lambda: pick(True, False))]:
        if r() < 0.45:
            p[k] = f()
    return p


calls = [('circuit', gen()) for _ in range(N)]
bad, outs = mcompare(calls, label='circuit wide sweep seed %d: ' % seed)
ok = sum(1 for x in outs if not x.startswith('ERR'))
print('   (%d of them sized, %d refused)' % (ok, len(outs) - ok))

"""Clean random layouts: orthogonal and slanted outlines of mixed wall types and location lines,
partitions ending on centre lines or faces, rooms in every region. usage: clean_test.py [N] [seed]"""
import sys, json, random, math
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/elec-agent')
from rooms_lib import build
from mlib import mbatch, ORIG, MINE
N = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 100
random.seed(int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 1)
TYPES = ['Generic - 200mm', 'Interior - 100mm', 'Exterior - 300mm']
LOCS = ['centre', 'core-centre', 'exterior-finish', 'interior-finish', 'exterior-core', 'interior-core']
NAMES = ['Sala', 'Quarto', 'Banheiro', 'Cozinha', 'Copa', 'Área de Serviço', 'Varanda', 'Hall', 'Suíte', 'Lavabo']
bad = tot = 0
for trial in range(N):
    W = random.choice([5000, 6000, 8000, 9000])
    H = random.choice([4000, 5000, 6000])
    kind = random.random()
    if kind < 0.4:
        outline = [[0, 0], [W, 0], [W, H], [0, H]]
    elif kind < 0.7:
        a = random.choice([0.4, 0.5, 0.6]) * W
        b = random.choice([0.4, 0.5, 0.6]) * H
        outline = [[0, 0], [W, 0], [W, b], [a, b], [a, H], [0, H]]
    else:
        s = random.choice([500, 1000, 1500])
        outline = [[0, 0], [W, 0], [W - s, H], [s, H]]
    if random.random() < 0.5:
        outline = outline[::-1]
    cmds = []
    t0 = random.choice(TYPES)
    l0 = random.choice(LOCS) if random.random() < 0.5 else 'centre'
    if random.random() < 0.5:
        cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": outline, "closed": True, "type": t0, "location": l0}))
    else:
        for k in range(len(outline)):
            cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": [outline[k], outline[(k + 1) % len(outline)]], "type": random.choice(TYPES), "location": l0}))
    rooms = []
    if kind < 0.4:
        # a partition across, ending on centre lines (or, with a centred outline, on the faces)
        x = random.choice([0.3, 0.5, 0.6]) * W
        ti = random.choice(TYPES)
        if l0 == 'centre' and random.random() < 0.5:
            half = {'Generic - 200mm': 100, 'Interior - 100mm': 50, 'Exterior - 300mm': 150}[t0]
            y0, y1 = half, H - half
        else:
            y0, y1 = 0, H
        cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": [[x, y0], [x, y1]], "type": ti}))
        rooms = [[x / 2, H / 2], [(x + W) / 2, H / 2]]
        if random.random() < 0.5:
            y = random.choice([0.4, 0.5]) * H
            cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": [[x, y], [W, y]], "type": random.choice(TYPES)}))
            rooms = [[x / 2, H / 2], [(x + W) / 2, y / 2], [(x + W) / 2, (y + H) / 2]]
    elif kind < 0.7:
        rooms = [[W * 0.15, H * 0.15]]
    else:
        rooms = [[W / 2, H / 2]]
    for q in rooms:
        cmds.append('room ' + json.dumps({"point": [round(q[0]), round(q[1])], "name": random.choice(NAMES)}, ensure_ascii=False))
    path = '/tmp/elec-agent/cl.bimcraft'
    try:
        build(cmds, path)
    except Exception as e:
        continue
    tot += 1
    a = mbatch(ORIG, [('load_points', {})], path)[0]
    b = mbatch(MINE, [('load_points', {})], path)[0]
    if a != b:
        bad += 1
        if bad <= 8:
            ja, jb = json.loads(a), json.loads(b)
            print('DIFF', json.dumps(cmds, ensure_ascii=False))
            print('   ORIG', [(r['name'], r['area_m2'], r['perimeter_m']) for r in ja['rooms']], [s['name'] for s in ja['skipped']])
            print('   MINE', [(r['name'], r['area_m2'], r['perimeter_m']) for r in jb['rooms']], [s['name'] for s in jb['skipped']])
print('clean layouts: %d, %d match, %d differ' % (tot, tot - bad, bad))

"""Writes random clean layouts (mixed wall types, location lines, partitions) with their room
points to a JSON file. usage: gen_layouts.py N seed out.json"""
import sys, json, random
N, seed, out = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]
random.seed(seed)
TYPES = ['Generic - 200mm', 'Interior - 100mm', 'Exterior - 300mm']
LOCS = ['centre', 'core-centre', 'exterior-finish', 'interior-finish', 'exterior-core', 'interior-core']
res = []
for trial in range(N):
    W = random.choice([4500, 5400, 6000, 7300, 8000, 9000])
    H = random.choice([3000, 4100, 5000, 6000])
    x0, y0 = random.choice([0, 1000, -2500]), random.choice([0, 700, -1200])
    pts = [[x0, y0], [x0 + W, y0], [x0 + W, y0 + H], [x0, y0 + H]]
    if random.random() < 0.3:
        pts = pts[::-1]
    loc = random.choice(LOCS) if random.random() < 0.4 else 'centre'
    cmds = []
    if random.random() < 0.5:
        cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": pts, "closed": True, "type": random.choice(TYPES), "location": loc}))
    else:
        for k in range(4):
            cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": [pts[k], pts[(k + 1) % 4]], "type": random.choice(TYPES), "location": loc}))
    rooms = [[x0 + W * 0.5, y0 + H * 0.5]]
    r = random.random()
    if r < 0.7:
        xp = x0 + random.choice([0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6]) * W
        cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": [[xp, y0], [xp, y0 + H]], "type": random.choice(TYPES)}))
        rooms = [[(x0 + xp) / 2, y0 + H / 2], [(xp + x0 + W) / 2, y0 + H / 2]]
        if random.random() < 0.6:
            yp = y0 + random.choice([0.3, 0.5, 0.6]) * H
            cmds.append('wall ' + json.dumps({"points": [[xp, yp], [x0 + W, yp]], "type": random.choice(TYPES)}))
            rooms = [[(x0 + xp) / 2, y0 + H / 2], [(xp + x0 + W) / 2, (y0 + yp) / 2], [(xp + x0 + W) / 2, (yp + y0 + H) / 2]]
    res.append([cmds, [[round(q[0]), round(q[1])] for q in rooms]])
json.dump(res, open(out, 'w'))

import math, itertools
# (loop points, thickness, location pos (from the left face), observed corners {index: (x, y)})
cases = [
    ([(0, 0), (7500, 0), (7500, 3500), (4500, 5000), (0, 5000)], 300.0, 150.0, {2: (7350.0, 3407.294901687516), 3: (4464.589803375, 4850.0)}),
    ([(0, 0), (6000, 0), (6000, 5600), (3600, 8000), (0, 8000)], 100.0, 50.0, {2: (5950.0, 5579.289321881346), 3: (3579.2893218813456, 7950.0)}),
    ([(0, 0), (6000, 0), (6000, 5600), (3600, 8000), (0, 8000)], 200.0, 100.0, {2: (5900.0, 5558.57864376269), 3: (3558.5786437626903, 7900.0)}),
    ([(0, 0), (6000, 0), (6000, 4200), (3600, 6000), (0, 6000)], 100.0, 100.0, {2: (5900.0, 4150.000000000011), 3: (3566.6666666666565, 5900.0)}),
]


def sub(a, b): return (a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1])
def add(a, b): return (a[0] + b[0], a[1] + b[1])
def mul(a, k): return (a[0] * k, a[1] * k)
def crs(a, b): return a[0] * b[1] - a[1] * b[0]


def faces(s, e, t, pos):
    d = sub(e, s)
    l = math.sqrt(d[0] * d[0] + d[1] * d[1])
    u = mul(d, 1.0 / l)
    nl = (-u[1], u[0])
    lo, ro = pos, t - pos
    left = (add(s, mul(nl, lo)), add(e, mul(nl, lo)))
    right = (add(s, mul(nl, -ro)), add(e, mul(nl, -ro)))
    return u, d, left, right


def F_pu(p, u, q, v):
    t = crs(sub(q, p), v) / crs(u, v)
    return add(p, mul(u, t))


def two_pt(a1, b1, a2, b2):
    x1, y1 = a1; x2, y2 = b1; x3, y3 = a2; x4, y4 = b2
    D = (x1 - x2) * (y3 - y4) - (y1 - y2) * (x3 - x4)
    px = ((x1 * y2 - y1 * x2) * (x3 - x4) - (x1 - x2) * (x3 * y4 - y3 * x4)) / D
    py = ((x1 * y2 - y1 * x2) * (y3 - y4) - (y1 - y2) * (x3 * y4 - y3 * x4)) / D
    return (px, py)


def candidates(w1, w2):
    """w1 ends at the joint, w2 starts there (a counter-clockwise loop: the room is on the left)."""
    u1, d1, l1, r1 = w1
    u2, d2, l2, r2 = w2
    out = {}
    # inner faces are the left ones
    out['pu: w1 end, u1; w2 start, u2'] = F_pu(l1[1], u1, l2[0], u2)
    out['pu: w2 start, u2; w1 end, u1'] = F_pu(l2[0], u2, l1[1], u1)
    out['pu away: w1 end,u1 ; w2 start,-u2'] = F_pu(l1[1], u1, l2[0], mul(u2, -1))
    out['pu: w1 start, d1; w2 start, d2'] = F_pu(l1[0], d1, l2[0], d2)
    out['pu: w1 end, d1; w2 start, d2'] = F_pu(l1[1], d1, l2[0], d2)
    out['pu: w2 start, d2; w1 end, d1'] = F_pu(l2[0], d2, l1[1], d1)
    out['pu: w2 start, d2; w1 start, d1'] = F_pu(l2[0], d2, l1[0], d1)
    out['pu: w1 start, u1; w2 start, u2'] = F_pu(l1[0], u1, l2[0], u2)
    out['pu: w2 end, u2; w1 start, u1'] = F_pu(l2[1], u2, l1[0], u1)
    out['pu: w1 start, u1; w2 end, u2'] = F_pu(l1[0], u1, l2[1], u2)
    out['2pt: w1(s,e) w2(s,e)'] = two_pt(l1[0], l1[1], l2[0], l2[1])
    out['2pt: w2(s,e) w1(s,e)'] = two_pt(l2[0], l2[1], l1[0], l1[1])
    out['2pt: w1(e,s) w2(s,e)'] = two_pt(l1[1], l1[0], l2[0], l2[1])
    out['2pt: w1(s,e) w2(e,s)'] = two_pt(l1[0], l1[1], l2[1], l2[0])
    out['2pt: w1(e,s) w2(e,s)'] = two_pt(l1[1], l1[0], l2[1], l2[0])
    return out


score = {}
for pts, t, pos, obs in cases:
    n = len(pts)
    ws = [faces(pts[k], pts[(k + 1) % n], t, pos) for k in range(n)]
    for idx, want in obs.items():
        w1 = ws[(idx - 1) % n]
        w2 = ws[idx]
        for name, got in candidates(w1, w2).items():
            ok = got == want
            score.setdefault(name, []).append(ok)
            if name.startswith('pu: w1 end, u1; w2 start, u2'):
                print(idx, want, got)
for name, oks in sorted(score.items(), key=lambda kv: -sum(kv[1])):
    print(sum(oks), len(oks), name)

content.text:
All three calculators are done and committed on branch `worktree-agent-a798dce38c11c4bb6` (commits `967d612`, `24237b8`, `6b20616`, `535fe02`, `b4ef201`, `8afe209`). `circuit` and `conduit_fill` match the original in every case I ran; `load_points` matches whenever rooms are given, and on model rooms it matches for clean layouts but still differs in a few unusual wall arrangements (listed below). The final full run of the sweep scripts in `/tmp/elec-agent/` all matched, and spot checks through the `run --cmd` path with `cmp.py` came out SAME.

| Command | What was checked | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `circuit` | 20,000 + 30,000 random parameter sets, plus 4,166 edge cases | all match |
| `conduit_fill` | 20,000 random, plus 3,010 exact-rounding-tie cases, plus 2,741 edge cases | all match |
| `load_points`, rooms given | 5,000 random sets, 2,415 name × kind combinations, 16 long-error cases | all match |
| `load_points`, model rooms | 77 fixed layouts, 120 mixed location-line layouts, 300 clean random, 300 general random (seed 12) | all match |

- **`circuit`:** every key, error text and the order of the checks; error clipping at 2000 characters.
  - All the NBR 5410 tables were read back from the original's outputs: 33, 36, 37, 40, 41, 42, 45, 47, 48 and 58, plus the breaker list.
  - Conductor resistances: flexible up to 240 mm², rigid × 1.07 above that, adjusted for 70 or 90 °C.
  - I reproduced the original's arithmetic order so the two-decimal rounding comes out the same.
- **`conduit_fill`:** I recovered the cable diameters and the inside diameter of each conduit size from the outputs. The fill is added up conductor by conductor, as the original does, so even exact rounding ties come out the same. A cable the catalogue lacks gives the same `pending` reply.
- **`load_points` with rooms given:** all error texts and check order. A room's own reading error is clipped before the `rooms[i]:` prefix is added, as the original does. Room kinds come from the name in Portuguese or English, ignoring accents and case; `wc`/`bwc`/`bath` must be whole words. When a name matches several kinds, service wins, then bath, kitchen, veranda and dry. Also matched: `counter_outlets`, the alternative, and empty sums printing `-0.0`.

**Stand-in for ARCH.** Walls, rooms and room separators aren't in our build yet, so `src/structure/calc/loads/rooms.rs` reads them from the saved project and measures each room inside the walls' finish. It handles:
- location lines, layered cores and the computation height;
- walls that don't bound rooms, and frozen rooms (they keep their saved boundary);
- arcs and islands;
- T-junctions, which cut the abutting wall on the other wall's face;
- corner joins;
- the rule that two rooms can't share one space.

On clean layouts it reproduces the original's boundaries to the last bit, so areas round the same way even at exact ties. It is private; ARCH can replace it with its own finish-measured boundary once rooms exist.

**Remaining `load_points` model-room differences.** About 1 in 100 general random layouts (6 of 600 across seeds 1 and 2) still came out 0.01–0.02 off, or skipped a room the original measures. These are:
- walls lying inside each other's thickness, or an island wall overlapping a partition;
- arc walls ending where two other walls meet, or crossing walls;
- one three-wall junction mix (layered and plain walls both on `exterior-core`).

Two smaller gaps:
- On slanted walls some vertices differ in the last floating-point digit. This only changes the output if an area lands exactly on a rounding tie, which slanted geometry practically never does.
- The vertex order inside a room's holes differs, which only matters for an exact tie in a room containing a free-standing wall.

**What others need to provide.** ARCH must save walls, rooms and room separators with the original's fields:
- walls: `start`, `end`, `type` (GUID), `location`, `arc`, `room_bounding`, `level`, `base_offset`, `height`, `top_level`, `top_offset`;
- levels: `computation_height`;
- rooms: `point`, `level`, `name`, `frozen`, `kept`;
- separators: `start`, `end`, `level`.

Nothing outside my files was changed, and I export no public functions for other parts.
